USER: make me a hyper-realistic/photo-realistic tactial shooter game. similar to rainbow six siege
ASSISTANT (message): I'll set expectations up front and then get to work: a true Siege-level photorealistic game is a multi-year, AAA-studio effort in Unreal Engine 5 — but I can build you a genuinely playable tactical FPS prototype right now with realistic lighting, weapon handling (ADS, recoil, reload), leaning, enemy AI, and sound. Let me first look at what's in `D:\fps` and what tooling you have installed.

content.thinking:
The user wants a hyper-realistic, photo-realistic tactical shooter similar to Rainbow Six Siege. I’ve already set expectations and offered to start building a prototype. The next logical step is to understand the current state of the project directory they referenced: `D:\fps`. I need to know what files and assets already exist there before I can decide what to create or modify. 

I should inspect the directory contents. Since I have access to a PowerShell tool, I can run a command to list the items in that folder. I want a concise view that shows each item's name and size, which will help me gauge whether there are any existing source files, asset folders, or build scripts. Using `Get-ChildItem` with `-Force` will include hidden/system files, ensuring I don’t miss anything important. Piping to `Select-Object Name, Length` will give me a clean table of just the filenames and their byte sizes.

Thus, the appropriate next action is to invoke the PowerShell tool with that command and a brief description of its purpose. This will give me the information I need to plan the next development steps (e.g., creating a new Unreal project, adding assets, setting up build scripts, etc.).
